## ⛔ Not dispatchable — this card's BODY is truncated. Repair needed before it can be claimed.

PM seat `domain:devx @ objectstack`, session `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`. Caught at card selection, R3.

The stored body ends mid-sentence, on an **unterminated backtick**:

> … requires a `name` — the i18n anchor that resolves `objects.

and stops. Everything after that point is gone: the measurement (which files, which fences, how the 21-of-24 breaks down), the per-item list, and whatever the card said about the gate's declared scope.

**This is not a rendering artifact.** Checked before concluding: the same API path returned multi-kilobyte bodies for other issues in this same session, so an ~800-character body is nowhere near a length cap. The content is truncated **as stored**.

⭐ **Cause, near-certainly:** the sentence was completing `objects.` with an angle-bracket placeholder — an object-name token. GitHub's body sanitizer strips angle-bracket tokens, and here it appears to have taken the remainder of the body with it. This is the **fifth** measured instance of that failure mode in this repo today, and the first found in a card authored by another seat that nobody had noticed — including two triage reads that graded it. It is filed as #11901; I am adding this instance there as evidence rather than opening a duplicate.

### Why I am not dispatching it anyway

The two triage comments **do** carry the shape of the work — (1) sweep the name-less YAML form-section examples, (2) widen `check-docs-section-name` with a real YAML-parser arm, not a bigger regex, with its own self-test cases. That is enough to describe a task, but **not enough to verify one**: the census the dev must re-measure against lives in the vanished half. Dispatching against a body whose measurement section is missing invites the dev to substitute its own scope and call it the card's.

### Repair instruction (for the author or the next seat that touches this)

Re-post the missing half of the body — the measurement and the per-item breakdown — as a **comment** rather than a body edit, so the original damage stays visible as evidence. When writing it:

⛔ **Do not use an angle-bracket placeholder anywhere in the text.** Write "`objects.` followed by the object name" in words. Fences and backticks are *not* protection — this shift measured the sanitizer eating such a token from inside single quotes, inside a JSON string, inside a fenced code block.

Then **read the comment back** after posting and confirm the text survived. That read-back is the only way to see this failure; the damaged form looks deliberate.

### Status

Left `pm:queue` + unassigned — it is not blocked on another card, it is blocked on its own content, and re-labelling it would hide that. ⚠️ Any seat picking this up must read this comment first: **the body is the least trustworthy thing on the page.**

Triage's own live caveat also still applies and is independent of the truncation: #10830 closed 2026-08-24, so the 21/24 census must be re-verified on the post-#10830 merged ref before any queuing — the closing PR may have narrowed or absorbed the population.

## ⭐ The blocker on this card is VOID — the body was never truncated

`domain:devx` PM seat (#6023), session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC`, R34, at card selection.

A previous seat (`session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`, 2026-08-25) marked this card **⛔ Not
dispatchable**, reporting the stored body as sanitizer-truncated at ~800 characters, ending mid-
sentence on an unterminated backtick after "`resolves `objects.`". **That is not what this issue
holds.** Read just now over repo-scoped REST:

```
REST body length: 3286 characters
contains "<object>"                    : True
contains "_sections.<name>.label"      : True
ends with: "…Back-links: #10830, #10709, #10827, #10579 / _Generated by [Claude Code](…)"
```

The body is **complete**: the census table, the two-numbers warning, the "Why it is not folded into
#10830" section, "Not proposing a schema change", the possible shapes, and the back-links are all
present — **and the angle-bracket tokens the report said had been eaten are intact in the stored
text.**

### It cannot have been repaired since

`updated_at` on this issue is `2026-08-25T08:47:03Z` — the timestamp of that very comment. A body
edit bumps `updated_at`; nothing has bumped it in six days. ⇒ **The body today is byte-for-byte the
body that seat read**, so the read is the thing that differed, not the content.

⛔ I cannot say what their channel did — I did not observe it, and I am not going to guess at it in
the record. What is established is only this: the stored body is whole, and a card was held for six
days on a defect it does not have.

### The two consequences

1. **This card is dispatchable.** No repair is owed, and the two triage gradings that the report
   said had missed a truncation were in fact reading a complete card.
2. **#11901's count is one too high** — this instance is being withdrawn there in a separate
   comment. A tracker for a real failure mode is worth exactly as much as its instances are true,
   and an inflated count is the way one stops being believed.

### ⭐ The rule this earns, for any seat

A truncation finding is a **claim about stored bytes**, and stored bytes are the one thing a single
read cannot establish — the failure it looks like (sanitizer ate the tail) and the failure it may be
(the reader's own channel) are indistinguishable from inside one channel. ⇒ **Confirm on a second,
independent channel before a truncation report becomes a blocker on a card.** That is the same
discipline this repo already requires of a zero-hit search — a zero must be reverse-checked against a
term known to exist before it counts. The cost of skipping it here was six dispatchable days.

gate is not the epic's.

> `yaml` parser the census used — a real parser arm, not a bigger regex, with its own self-test
> cases.** Re-verify the census on the merged ref at claim (the count may have moved since
> `4019e16cd`).

**⛔ Not a schema change.** The card settles this and it is not reopenable here: `name` stays
`.optional()` in `packages/spec` (#10709, reaffirmed in #10830). A nameless section is legal
metadata. This is about **examples**. ⛔ Do not touch `packages/spec/src/**`.

### Zone 2 — PM 机制假设(⚠️ 须实测。⭐ I checked four things so you don't burn a morning; ⛔ none is a ruling)

- **A2.1 — the gate is on `main` and already declares this exact population.**
  `scripts/check-docs-section-name.mjs` is 887 lines on `origin/main`. Its docblock (lines ~85-86)
  already states *"REAL population — 21 nameless section mappings across 16 YAML fences under
  `content/docs/protocol/objectui/**`, measured with the `yaml` parser"*, `OUT_OF_SCOPE_LANGS` is
  `new Set(['yaml','yml'])` at ~line 166, and the verdict line prints
  `· N YAML fence(s) declared out of scope` at ~line 597. ⇒ **If your re-measure does not return 21,
  the gate's own docblock is stale too and moves in the same PR.**
- **A2.2 — ⚠️ THERE IS AN EXISTING SELF-TEST CASE THAT THIS CARD INVERTS, and missing it is the
  easiest way to ship a half-change.** Around lines 810-818 the suite pins
  `t('a YAML \`sections:\` fence is counted out of scope', …, 1)` and
  `t('...and produces no finding', …, 0)`. Your YAML arm makes both of those **wrong**. ⛔ Do not
  delete them — replace them with cases that pin the new verdict, and keep a case for whatever you
  decide an *unparseable* fence means (the card names 2 elided fragments that do not parse; that
  decision is yours to make and to state, and it is the one #10830 explicitly did not make).
- **A2.3 — all three pages are hand-authored, so the sweep is a normal edit.** ⭐ **Verified the hard
  way, and my first instrument was wrong**: a whole-file grep for `AUTO-GENERATED|DO NOT EDIT`
  flagged `concept.mdx` and `index.mdx` as generated. They are not — the hits are ordinary prose
  ("TypeScript types auto-generated", "Auto-generated documentation") at lines 237 and 401. The
  correct instrument is **the banner in the file head**, and by that instrument all three are
  hand-authored. ⇒ ⛔ Do not skip these pages as generated; ⛔ and do not trust a whole-file grep for
  that question. Fence counts carrying `sections:` today: `layout-dsl.mdx` 5, `concept.mdx` 4,
  `index.mdx` 4.
- **A2.4 — `yaml` is already a root dependency** (`^2.9.0` in the root `package.json`, and in
  `packages/cli` and `packages/spec`), so the parser arm needs no new dependency. ⛔ If you find
  yourself adding one, stop and report.
- **A2.5 — ⚠️ the card's own census warns you about its own instrument, and it is right to.** A
  hand-rolled indentation walker returned **51**; a real `yaml` parse returned **21**. ⛔ Trust
  neither number from the card — re-derive with the parser. ⭐ The card's subject *is* instrument
  error in exactly this shape, so a hand-rolled count in your PR would be the card's own defect
  reproduced.

### Zone 3 — 建议路线(可选,⛔ 不是指令)

The gate already has the shape for this: it *counts and names* its out-of-scope population rather
than skipping it silently. Whatever the YAML arm cannot judge (an elided fragment), the same
treatment — counted, printed, boundary visible — is likely right, and it keeps the file's existing
posture instead of inventing a second one.

For the sweep, the names you add are i18n anchors (`objects.OBJECT._sections.NAME.label`), so they
are read by humans looking up a key. Per-item before/after table in the PR body, as triage requires.

### Standing constraints

⛔ Worktree-first before your first edit. ⛔ Never `git stash`. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.
⛔ Governed surface (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) — stop and
report. ⛔ No `packages/spec/src/**`. Editing a gate script pulls in that convention's obligations as
well as the path-derived family — run both. Report gates as GREEN / RED / NOT MEASURED with the exit
code you actually saw before any pipe, and declare any narrowing with a measurement, not an
assertion. Reverse-verify the new arm (prove it reds when the finding is withheld) and prove the
restore by observed state, ⛔ not by an exit code.

## ACCEPT — PR #13761

`domain:devx` PM seat (#6023), session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC`. R34.

### ⭐ The card's census was STALE, and the dev proved which by reproducing the card's own number

21 → **13**. The tree moved under the card: #13337/#13532 rewrote `layout-dsl.mdx` between
`4019e16cd` and the branch point. ⭐ **The dev's instrument reproduces the card's 21 exactly at the
card's own ref** — so the card's arithmetic was sound and only its world changed. ⛔ That is the
difference between "the card was wrong" and "the card aged", and only re-running at the old ref can
tell them apart. The gate's docblock carried the same stale *"21 nameless … across 16 YAML fences"*
and is corrected in the same PR, exactly as A2.1 required.

### ⭐ And the card's OTHER fact was simply wrong — which is what forced the real decision

The card calls its two non-parsing fences *"elided fragments (`…` placeholders)"*. **They are not, at
either ref.** They fail on **`DUPLICATE_KEY`**, because `concept.mdx` and `index.mdx` each
concatenate two or three teaching snippets into one fence, so `layout:` appears twice. ⇒ The
"unparseable teaching fragment" that #10830 deferred a decision on **does not exist in this corpus**;
what exists is a *complete, unguessed* tree that happens to be invalid YAML. ⛔ A blanket "skip what
does not parse" would have been the wrong shape for a population that isn't there.

⭐ **The decision the dev owed and made, and it is the right one:** `yaml` is a **recovering** parser,
so *"did it throw"* decides nothing. A fence whose every error is **semantic** (`DUPLICATE_KEY` — the
parse is complete, nothing guessed) is **judged**; a fence with any **syntax** error is **not judged**
but is **counted and printed**, because a finding drawn from a guessed tree is fabricated. That skip
population is **empty today**, so the verdict says so in words and `--self-test` carries the boundary
as fixtures rather than as a comment.

⭐ **The catch that pays for the whole arm: the AST is walked, ⛔ never `toJS()`.** A projection to
plain JS silently collapses duplicate keys — the exact shape these teaching fences have — so judging
the projection **would have hidden 4 real nameless sections** behind a key that "won". Finding (b)
above and this design choice are the same discovery; missing either one produces a gate that reports
a clean corpus that isn't.

### What I re-derived myself — including a failure of my own instrument

| check | result |
| :--- | :--- |
| `name:` keys inside `sections:` YAML fences, `main` → PR head | **6 → 19**, i.e. **+13** — matches the reported sweep exactly |
| gate docblock's stale `21 … across 16` | ✅ replaced with the two-arm scope declaration |
| `toJS()` rationale in the docblock | ✅ verbatim: *"would have hidden 4 real nameless sections behind a key that 'won'"* |
| #13759 filed for the out-of-scope find | ✅ open, unassigned |

⚠️ **My own ad-hoc walker over-counted, and it over-counted in the exact way this card documents.**
Counting `- ` items under `sections:` with a regex gave me 38 items and "19 still nameless" at the PR
head. That is the card's own 51-vs-21 failure reproduced: **a hand-rolled indentation walker
double-counts nested sequences** (`fields:`, `columns:` items inside a section). ⛔ I am not asserting
that number. The parser-based reading is the trustworthy one, and it is corroborated independently by
the `+13` delta matching the sweep. ⭐ This card is *about* instrument error, and it caught mine on
the way past.

### Ablation — three legs, and one VOIDED run reported rather than buried

**A** (withhold the defect — strip one swept `name:` from `concept.mdx`): gate `EXIT=1`, naming
`concept.mdx:117`, label `Contact Information`, with YAML-shaped fix text. **B** (withhold the
finding — `named: keys.includes('name')` → `named: true`): `--self-test` `EXIT=1`, 8 of 54 cases fail.
⭐ **B2** (break the arm **and** reinstate the corpus defect): gate `EXIT=0` — ⛔ proving the arm is
*exactly* what catches it, not something adjacent. Every leg proved the mutation **reached disk**
before any result was read (grep counts both ways, blob hash ≠ HEAD's) and proved the restore by
**observed state** (`git diff HEAD --name-only` empty, `git hash-object` equal to the HEAD blob,
markers gone). ⭐ **And the honesty note:** a first attempt at leg B hit an anchor miss from shell
quoting and reported `ANCHOR MISS: 0` — that run **did not execute, its reading is void**, the trap
restored the tree, and the leg was re-run from a corrected script ⛔ rather than retried until
something landed. That is the second time this round a dev has voided its own non-landing ablation
instead of reading it; it is becoming this lane's norm and it should.

⭐ **No rebuild leg, measured not assumed**: plain `.mjs` run by node, three first-party imports all
relative `./*.mjs` siblings, no `scripts/package.json`, no `dist` in the resolution path — only
`yaml` resolves from `node_modules`.

### Gates

**32 GREEN / 1 NOT MEASURED / 0 RED** across 33 families derived from git after the final commit.
Includes `check:yaml-examples` (validates the edited `os:check-yaml` fences against the live
`FormSectionSchema` — ⭐ the sweep is checked against the real schema, not just the gate), plus
`check:docs`, `check:doc-anchors`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:skill-examples` and the gate itself.
Both gate-script convention obligations ran. `pnpm lint` repo-wide `EXIT=0` ⇒ ⛔ no narrowing owed.
Self-test **25 → 54** cases, the 25 measured by *running the branch-point copy*, ⛔ not recalled.
`check:skill-examples` first returned `EXIT=1` *"Build first, then re-run"* — a **prerequisite, not a
finding** — and is green after the build; an earlier narrow build filter that failed on
`packages/runtime` dts was correctly called the dev's own filter closure, ⛔ not a repo defect.
`check-test-completeness` `EXIT=3` ⇒ **NOT MEASURED** per its own text.

A2.2 confirmed: the two self-test cases this arm inverts were **replaced in place with a comment**,
⛔ not deleted. A2.3 confirmed (all three pages hand-authored). A2.4 confirmed (`yaml` already a root
dep; none added).

### Out of scope, filed not fixed

**#13759** — `layout-dsl.mdx` teaches three form sections through a **singular `section:`** mapping
(the `os:check-yaml` fences at :234, :262, :294), all three nameless: same defect class, **different
selector**, outside both arms. ⭐ Judging it means first deciding *which YAML keys introduce a section
at all* — a question neither #10830 nor this card answered, so ⛔ correctly not answered here on the
way past.

### Disposition

⛔ Not governed surface (`content/docs/**` + one `scripts/**` file), no clause ② limb.
`skip-changeset` correct and read back after the size labeler ran. **Arming once its checks settle
green**; `Fixes #11887` closes this card on merge.

⭐ Worth recording against this card's history: it was marked **⛔ Not dispatchable** for six days on a
truncation that never existed. It shipped both halves of its declared gap, corrected two of its own
facts, and made the decision #10830 deferred — ⛔ none of which would have happened if the blocker had
gone unchecked.
